card.name: Linking words before a restriction or caution
card.fires_on: Small linking or auxiliary words (unless, are, until, be, not, is) in the middle of a sentence, right before a condition, limit or caution is stated. Seen in drug-label instructions and warnings.

modes.label: Auxiliary after should not / would / could
modes.description: The word be after a modal such as should not, would or could, before a participle like used, exceeded or problematic.
modes.example: epinephrine and dopamine should not<< be>> used, since beta stimulation combined with α

modes.label: Condition or limit words
modes.description: Words like unless, until or not that introduce an exception or limit.
modes.example: RETEVMO may be taken with or without food<< unless>> coadministered with a proton pump

modes.label: Verb before a risk statement
modes.description: Are or is linking a subject to an association with risk or a recommendation against use.
modes.example: for which elevated plasma concentrations<< are>> associated with serious and/or life-threatening reactions

card.writes: It lowers negative-outcome words (harm, loss, adverse, worsening), mostly in Chinese, so it seems to steer away from that kind of continuation.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words just before a label states an exception, limit or caution.
